answer: Each agent earns a reputation score by staking tokens that decay like a vine’s growth: early contributions are weighted quadratically, so a thousand fresh identities each gain only √1/1000 of the base weight. When a new node whispers a transaction, the network queries a decentralized lagoon of anchored proofs; only identities whose cumulative weighted stake surpasses a threshold can validate. An attacker must acquire enough native tokens to amplify many Sybil nodes, turning the cost from linear to quadratic in the number of fake IDs.
